package_info.package_manager: N/A (delivered via Smoke Loader, not a public package repository)
package_info.why_malicious: Whiffy Recon is considered malicious because it is a geo-location malware that persistently scans for nearby Wi-Fi networks, leverages the Google Geolocation API to determine the victim's physical location, and exfiltrates this data to attacker-controlled infrastructure, enabling covert, ongoing surveillance and severe privacy violations.

execution_context.trigger: at runtime (post-infection, upon execution of Whiffy Recon payload)
execution_context.file_location: main malware payload (delivered by Smoke Loader, typically in a temporary or user profile directory)
required_permissions: network (for external API and C2 communication)
filesystem (for persistence and possible log storage)

malicious_snippets.code_language: pseudo-code (actual malware observed in C++/C# variants)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code continuously scans for nearby Wi-Fi networks, submits the collected Wi-Fi data to the Google Geolocation API to resolve the device's physical location, and exfiltrates the resulting geolocation data to a remote command-and-control server, enabling persistent, covert tracking of the victim.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs continuous Wi-Fi scanning and automated geolocation resolution, then exfiltrates precise location data to an external server without user knowledge or consent. This behavior is highly indicative of surveillance malware and is not found in legitimate applications outside of explicit, user-approved location services.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not repeatedly scan for Wi-Fi networks or send geolocation data to external servers without clear user consent and visible purpose. Legitimate use of geolocation APIs is typically event-driven and transparent to the user, not persistent and covert.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate location-based services (such as mapping or ride-sharing apps) may use Wi-Fi scanning and geolocation APIs, but only after obtaining explicit user permission and only for the duration of a user-initiated action. They do not perform continuous, background tracking or exfiltrate data to unknown servers.
key_indicators: Continuous, automated Wi-Fi network scanning by a non-network management process
Programmatic, repeated requests to the Google Geolocation API from an unknown binary
Regular exfiltration of geolocation data to hardcoded or dynamically resolved C2 endpoints
Operation in the background without user interaction or visible notification
Persistence mechanisms to ensure malware restarts after reboot (e.g., registry run keys, scheduled tasks)

attack_chain.action: Initial infection occurs via Smoke Loader, which downloads and executes the Whiffy Recon payload on the victim system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of Whiffy Recon malware on the victim system

attack_chain.action: Whiffy Recon executes and begins continuous scanning of nearby Wi-Fi networks to collect environmental data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of Wi-Fi network data from the victim's environment

attack_chain.action: The collected Wi-Fi network data is sent to the Google Geolocation API to determine the victim's physical location.
attack_chain.leads_to: Acquisition of the victim's geolocation coordinates

attack_chain.action: The victim's geolocation data is exfiltrated to the attacker's command-and-control server for ongoing surveillance.
attack_chain.leads_to: Persistent tracking and surveillance of the victim by the attacker

behavioral_signatures: Continuous or periodic Wi-Fi network scanning by processes that are not legitimate network management tools
Automated, repeated queries to the Google Geolocation API from unknown or unsigned binaries
Regular exfiltration of geolocation data to external IPs or domains not associated with legitimate services
Background operation of unknown executables with persistence mechanisms (e.g., registry run keys, scheduled tasks)
file_indicators: Presence of unknown executables delivered by Smoke Loader in temporary or user profile directories
Malware persistence mechanisms such as registry run keys (e.g., HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run) or scheduled tasks referencing Whiffy Recon payload
Unusual binaries with no digital signature or with anomalous metadata
network_indicators: Frequent outbound connections to Google Geolocation API endpoints (e.g., www.googleapis.com/geolocation/v1/geolocate)
Outbound connections to known C2 infrastructure associated with Whiffy Recon or Smoke Loader (as identified in threat intelligence feeds)
Unusual POST requests containing geolocation data to non-Google domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for processes that repeatedly scan for Wi-Fi networks and make automated requests to the Google Geolocation API. Correlate this activity with outbound traffic to suspicious or known C2 domains. Flag unknown binaries delivered by Smoke Loader, especially those establishing persistence via registry or scheduled tasks. Use behavioral analytics to detect continuous geolocation exfiltration and background operation of unsigned executables. Cross-reference with threat intelligence to identify C2 infrastructure.
